access.edition_or_version: The Pillow Book, trans. Meredith McKinney (Penguin Classics, 2006)

mechanics.tone_relevance: Non-Anglophone anchor for disclosed interiority: private observations, lists, and complaints make a court woman's inner life available to the reader.
mechanics.point_of_view: First person, present-tense observation and opinion; the narrating self does not explain or justify itself.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Lists ('things that...'), vignettes, gossip, aesthetic judgments; compendium structure with abrupt shifts.
mechanics.imagery: Minute sensory and social detail rather than abstract reflection.
mechanics.intimacy_technique: Closeness is produced by unguarded opinion and private register rather than by a dramatic confession.
mechanics.boundary_caveat: The work was intended privately and accidentally circulated; its public/private status is contested, so it evidences disclosed interiority more strongly than explicit addressedness.
mechanics.translation_note: Heian Japanese honorifics and poetic allusion are only partly recoverable in English.
mechanics.copyright_note: Translation copyrighted; original work public domain. Techniques described, no text reproduced.
